concept.name: Three outside down
concept.definition: A three-candlestick bearish reversal pattern introduced by Gregory Morris as a confirmed bearish engulfing: a white body in an uptrend is engulfed by a larger black body (the engulfing), and then a third black candle closes below the second candle's close. The third candle's lower close confirms the engulfing signal; it is the mirror of three outside up.
concept.intuition: Sellers first swallow the prior up candle whole, then prove it was no fluke by closing lower again the very next session.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: candle 1 is a white body; candle 2 is a long black body engulfing body 1 (O2 >= C1, C2 <= O1); candle 3 is a black candle closing below C2. Shadows are disregarded. Higher-than-usual volume on the third candle is considered supportive.
concept.formula: Three outside down when C1 > O1, O2 >= C1, C2 <= O1, C2 < O2, and C3 < C2 (with candle 3 black).
concept.failure_modes: In strong uptrends the confirmed pattern still fails often as the dip is bought; scan statistics show a meaningful fraction of false signals. Entering after the third candle can also place the stop far away, hurting risk-reward.
concept.misconceptions: It is not simply a bearish engulfing; the confirming third candle is part of the definition. Like the other Morris extensions, it is a modern formalization rather than a classical Japanese pattern.
concept.example: In an uptrend, a stock prints a white candle (70.00 to 72.00), a long black candle engulfing it (72.30 to 69.50), then a third black candle closing at 68.80. The three outside down is read as a confirmed bearish reversal.
